abstract: Filamentous microorganisms-encompassing filamentous fungi and actinomycetes-are versatile cell factories for producing proteins and bioactive natural products, playing a critical role in the food and pharmaceutical industries. These microorganisms exhibit slow growth and complex morphological differentiation. Conventional screening methods for strain engineering are hindered by low throughput and an inability to resolve heterogeneity in strain cultivation and growth. Droplet-based microfluidics offers an attractive platform for high-throughput screening at the single-cell level, yet its utility is limited by poor droplet stability and low post-sorting viability. Given the aforementioned technical bottlenecks, this study aims to compare the compatibility between filamentous fungi and actinomycetes and droplet microfluidic technology, optimize post-sorting strain viability, and thereby establish a droplet microfluidic screening platform applicable to diverse filamentous microorganisms. Here, we systematically evaluated and optimized droplet-based microfluidic screening for filamentous fungi-Acremonium chrysogenum and two actinomycetes, Streptomyces lividans and Saccharopolyspora erythraea. Monodisperse spore-suspension preparation protocols and droplet incubation time were optimized for each organism, which revealed that actinomycete-generated droplets were significantly more stable than those of filamentous fungi, with optimal sorting windows dictated by strain-specific growth and morphological traits. Subsequently, we varied sorting voltage and recovery regimens (no treatment, demulsification, or demulsification followed by shaking incubation). Lower sorting voltage markedly improved viability, while demulsification effectively boosted viability. These targeted optimizations establish a practical workflow that converts droplet-based microfluidics into a robust tool for high-throughput screening of filamentous microorganisms.

ChinaSheng Wu Gong Cheng Xue Bao94264631000-3061IMFungigrowth & developmentisolation & purificationMicrofluidic Analytical TechniquesmethodsMicrofluidicsmethodsActinobacteriagrowth & developmentHigh-Throughput Screening Assaysmethods丝状微生物(丝状真菌、放线菌)具有强大的生产蛋白和生物活性天然产物的能力，在食品、医药等领域具有不可替代的重要作用。这类微生物生长缓慢、形态分化复杂，传统筛选方法在进行菌株改造时存在通量低、难以区分菌株培养与生长发育异质性等瓶颈。液滴微流控技术为其单细胞水平筛选提供了新途径，却面临液滴稳定性不足、分选后菌株存活率偏低的问题。鉴于上述技术瓶颈，本研究旨在比较丝状真菌与放线菌对液滴微流控技术的适配性，优化分选后菌株存活率，从而建立适配多类丝状微生物的液滴微流控筛选技术体系。本研究以丝状真菌顶头孢霉(Acremonium chrysogenum)和2种丝状放线菌——变铅青链霉菌(Streptomyces lividans)、红色糖多孢菌(Saccharopolyspora erythraea)为研究对象，系统探究液滴微流控筛选中丝状微生物的适配性及存活率优化策略。通过优化单分散孢子悬液制备方法与液滴培养时间，分析不同丝状微生物液滴稳定性的差异及最佳分选时机。此外，还考察了不同分选电压与再生处理方式(无处理、破乳、破乳后振荡孵育)对分选后各菌株存活率的影响。结果表明，丝状放线菌的液滴稳定性显著优于丝状真菌;不同菌株的最佳分选时间因其生长和形态特性而异;低电压分选更有利于丝状微生物分选后的存活，且破乳处理可显著提升菌株存活率。本研究通过针对性优化筛选条件实现了菌株存活率的提升，为液滴微流控技术在丝状微生物高通量筛选中的应用提供了技术支撑。.droplet stabilitydroplet-based microfluidicsfilamentous microorganismhigh-throughput screeningpost-sorting viability作者声明没有任何可能会影响本文所报告工作的已知经济利益或个人关系。202692353620269235352026923133ppublish4277367210.13345/j.cjb.2601261000-3061(2026)09-4225-14ZHANG LH, ZHENG XM, CAIRNS TC, ZHANG ZD, WANG DP, ZHENG P, SUN JB.
